subject: Batching & KV-cache + Quantization — pricing and packaging decision tree
body:
From: Amit Shah <amit@nebula.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Initial ask — batching/KV-cache + quantization pricing for a 3-month pilot

Hi Priya,

Thanks for taking this. Were running a small ML infra team at NebulaAI evaluating inference vendors for our multi-tenant semantic search product. Two quick things we need before we sync:

1) A short table comparing expected per-token unit economics for three approaches: cache-first (heavy KV cache reuse), batch-optimized (high throughput, larger seqs), and quantized (int8 / 4-bit) at our scale.
2) Typical packaging you offer for a 3-month pilot (credits, commitment, and any conditional discounts for annual conversion).

For context: baseline QPS ~120 peak, avg tokens/request ~700, 99th latency SLO = 350ms (p95 is ~120ms today). Were open to a short pilot (3 months, limited dataset) and want a mutual action plan. Dana (ccd) is our procurement lead and will review terms.

Can you send a short decision tree / pricing scenarios we can review?

Cheers,
Amit
Amit Shah
Head of Infra, NebulaAI

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit@nebula.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — batching/KV-cache + quantization pricing for a 3-month pilot

Hi Amit — great context, thanks. I pulled together three pragmatic commercial options and a short technical note so you can map cost to risk/latency. Attaching a one-pager (batching-kv-options.pdf). High-level: 

- Cache-first path: prioritize KV/prefix reuse. Best for conversational or reuse-heavy workloads. Expect up to 4x token savings in steady-state on repeat prefixes. Lower ingress QPS required; slightly higher headroom needed for cache warming.

- Batch-optimal path: group small requests to maximize GPU utilization. Lowers per-token unit cost for throughput-bound workloads; better for large batched inference. May add 10-40ms scheduling latency for micro-batches depending on target SLO.

- Quantization-first path: use aggressive quant (int8 -> dynamic-4bit) for the same model variants. Biggest wins on GPU memory and cost per token but requires validation for any quality-sensitive prompts (we provide eval hooks).

Commercial sketches we propose for a 3-month pilot (examples):
- Flex pilot: $10k credits/month, pay-as-you-go overage, no upfront commit.
- Committed pilot: $22k/month with a 2x committed credit; nets 15% off list in pilot phase.
- Proof + Convert: $40k upfront credits for 3 months + 12-month conversion credit at 20% discount on committed tiers. Add-on: additional 5% reference discount if NebulaAI publishes a short blurb (optional).

Two asks from our side to firm up numbers:
1) Can you confirm expected average tokens/day and any seasonality?
2) Which models/architectures you want to test (or would you like us to recommend a few)?

Next step: Ill book a 30-min call with Karthik to scope the technical fit and a quick procurement sync with Dana.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
Attachment: batching-kv-options.pdf (PDF, 1 page)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit@nebula.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 08:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — batching/KV-cache + quantization pricing for a 3-month pilot

Amit / Priya — quick technical note to help map the commercial options to trade-offs. Ill also attach a short quant roadmap (quant-roadmap.xlsx). Key bullets: 

- If 99th SLO is 350ms, cache-first is safest. KV cache hits today will keep tail latency low because we avoid re-populating KV for repeated contexts. If youre at ~700 tokens/request, our measurements show ~30-45% token reduction at ~60% hit rates.

- Batch-optimal will reduce $/token when you can tolerate a 20-40ms queuing increase. For your 120 QPS peak, batching windows of 10-20ms give good utilization without large tail risk.

- Quantization: FP16 -> int8 typically reduces GPU memory 2x and cost ~28% in our infra. Dynamic 4-bit (group-wise) can further reduce costs but requires prompt-sensitivity testing: we recommend a two-week eval with a 50k prompt sample.

Recommended approach (technical decision tree):
1) Start cache-first for first 2-4 weeks to measure hit rates and establish realistic steady-state tokens.
2) Introduce conservative batching (10ms window) for non-99th-sensitive routes.
3) Run quant eval on a shadow set and only flip quantized model for low-risk routes once quality loss < 1.5% on your eval metric.

Ops note: For committed pilots, we can pre-configure a mixed routing policy so you can flip strategies without redeploying model variants.

-Karthik
Attachment: quant-roadmap.xlsx (XLSX, 5 sheets)

Subject: Re: Initial ask — batching/KV-cache + quantization pricing for a 3-month pilot

Thanks Priya/Karthik — this is helpful. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- Our average tokens/day: ~18M, peak day has hit 45M historically for search bursts.
- Model plan: currently running a 7B decoder-only open model in staging; willing to try a smaller 3B variant if you recommend it for quant tests.
- Procurement question: if we move to a 12-month committed contract after the pilot, what incremental discount bands do you have for banded commits (e.g., $200k / $500k / $1M annual commit)? Any SLA credits for latency breaches?

Dana is on cc to coordinate terms. Wed like a simple table: commit-band -> effective $/1M tokens at int8 + batch-mix + KV-hit assumptions. Also curious about how Redwood handles fallback if quantized variant fails an eval in production (automatic rollback?).

Appreciate a pricing scenario and a quick draft MAP (mutual action plan).

Amit

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Initial ask — batching/KV-cache + quantization pricing for a 3-month pilot

Hi Amit / Dana — thanks for the numbers. Attached Ive added a CSV with three concrete pricing scenarios (pricing-scenarios.csv) mapping commit-bands to effective $/1M tokens under three operational mixes (cache-first, batch-mix, quantized-int8). TL;DR: 

- $200k ARR band: 12% discount off list; effective $/1M tokens (cache-first) ~$420; int8 mix ~$300.
- $500k ARR band: 18% discount; effective $/1M tokens (cache-first) ~$360; int8 mix ~$255.
- $1M+ ARR band: 25% discount; effective $/1M tokens (cache-first) ~$320; int8 mix ~$220.

SLA / credits: we offer a 99.9% uptime SLA on Dedicated plans. For hosted pilots, we provide best-effort SLOs; on a paid conversion we will include latency SLO credits (service credits tiered by violation severity) in the committed contract.

Fallbacks: Redwoods rollout hooks include automatic rollback to the prior model variant on quality regressions (we can set a threshold metric and enable automatic revert). That behavior is configurable per-route.

Pilot offer we recommend for NebulaAI: 
1) 3-month committed pilot: $30k/month billed as upfront $90k credit. Includes 50k eval-run tokens for quant testing and a 2-week priority onboarding slot.
2) Conversion commitment if signed within 30 days of pilot close: 18% discount at $500k ARR band + a one-time onboarding credit equivalent to 10% of pilot cost.

Next steps: Ill share the CSV and a 30-min MAP doc. Proposed time to sync with your infra + procurement: Thu 4 Jun, 10:00am PT. If that works, Ill send a calendar invite.

If helpful, internal note to Karthik (quoted below) — please prep the quant eval template and a short runbook for rollback thresholds so we can share with Dana during procurement.

> Priya Natarajan wrote:
> Karthik — can you prepare the two-week eval template + a short SLA clause draft for pilot->commit conversion? Aim for rollback thresholds: quality delta < 1.5% and latency tail within 20% of baseline.
>
Thanks all — looking forward to the call.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
